text: Lithography puts the ridges on the chips. We can reduce the feature size, but then customers complain there's nowhere for the flavour to sit.
Resist development determines the curl of the chips. We shortened the process to save money and now procurement has to buy bendier potatoes.
We're on a 3 nm process. Three corners per Dorito. I've updated the investor deck.
Our prototype uses chocolate chips. They're cheaper, and if the thermal tests fail I can eat the evidence.
Pringles arrive as stacked wafers. I've assigned the man on the tube with a moustache to advanced packaging.

Our chocolate-chip RAM melted. That's phase-change memory, procurement forgot the new phase is a puddle.
